title: NoteCrate — Pipeline Overview
description: Plan 3.6: end-to-end query latency (p50/p95), retrieval latency, generation latency, error rate, request volume. Per-stage panels come from src/metrics.py.

panels.title: Query latency p50 / p95
panels.description: End-to-end /query latency. Warm single-user baseline on the staging VM is ~5.5s; the full eval set averages 8.3s. Under concurrency this diverges sharply from the per-stage panel — a p95 of 87s was measured at 5 VUs while the stages themselves summed to ~21s. That gap is queueing, not work: the box serves 1-2 concurrent users before contention dominates.

panels.title: Per-stage latency (p95)
panels.description: Where the time actually goes. retrieve = hybrid search + cross-encoder rerank; verify = per-sentence NLI; generate = Ollama on the host GPU. Healthy on the 4-core staging VM, warm: retrieve ~1.5s, generate ~2s, verify ~2s. retrieve climbing past ~5s usually means multi-hop routing fired (one rerank pass per sub-query). verify scales with answer LENGTH, not question difficulty, so it is the noisiest of the three.

panels.title: Error rate (5xx)
panels.description: 5xx only. 401 and 404 are excluded deliberately — a rejected login and a refused question are the system working, not failing.

panels.title: Refusals (gate)
panels.description: Questions declined at the noise floor before generation ran. Non-zero is healthy — it means the corpus boundary is being enforced. A sudden climb usually means the floor needs re-fitting after a corpus change.

panels.title: Grounding ratio (mean)
panels.description: Mean fraction of answer sentences TAGGED `grounded` — which is not the same as the fraction that ARE. Tag accuracy is ~0.54 against the labelled set, so read this as a trend line: a sharp drop is meaningful, the absolute value is not. Note it also moves when the tagger changes: cutting premises 3->2 raised accuracy while LOWERING this number, because the tagger became more conservative.

panels.title: API logs
panels.description: Centralized via Loki/Promtail, so a single query can be traced without SSH-ing into containers.
